body:
@sepo-agent /answer

Please investigate an inconsistency in the answer-route footer / template metadata. I expected these two Sepo answers to use the same answer template and display model metadata consistently:

- #396 initial issue mention answer: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/396#issuecomment-4606994467
  - run: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/actions/runs/26847747552
  - footer: `codex` | `gpt-5.5/xhigh` | `Macmini-runner-1`
- #395 implicit follow-up answer: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/395#issuecomment-4606983913
  - run: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/actions/runs/26847712984
  - footer: `codex` | `gpt-5.5` | `high` | `Macmini-runner-5`

Questions:

1. Are both actually using `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md`, or does the implicit follow-up path use a different answer template/context?
2. Why does one footer encode reasoning in the model (`gpt-5.5/xhigh`) while the other shows model and reasoning separately (`gpt-5.5` | `high`)?
3. Is this due to fresh vs resumed sessions, the `followup-intent` gate, or inconsistent reasoning-effort defaults between dispatch/answer paths?
4. If it is just display metadata, please propose how to normalize it so answer-route comments show the same footer shape across explicit and implicit follow-up runs.

No implementation needed yet; first please investigate and explain the root cause / recommended fix.

Moved out from https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/396#issuecomment-4607347766 so #396 can stay focused on issue-scoped `/review` routing.

comments.body:
Investigated. This is a display-normalization issue, with resumed answer sessions making it show up.

1. Both final comments used `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md`.

The referenced runs both entered the same final `agent / answer` job with:

- `prompt: answer`
- `route: answer`
- `session_policy: resume-best-effort`

In the runtime, `answer` maps to `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md` here:

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L125-L132

The implicit follow-up path does run an extra portal gate first:

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L350-L386

That gate uses `prompt: followup-intent`, but only to decide `respond` vs `ignore`. The posted answer is still produced later by the normal answer job:

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L537-L571

So: same final answer template, different pre-routing path.

2. The footer differs because it mixes ACP-reported model metadata with workflow reasoning metadata.

Footer construction does this:

- extract model from the ACP session log if present
- otherwise fall back to requested `MODEL_ID`
- include `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT` unless the model string already has a Codex reasoning suffix like `/xhigh`

Relevant code:

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L289-L320

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L322-L340

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L632-L640

The observed logs line up with that:

- #396 was a fresh answer session. The session log reported `gpt-5.5/xhigh`, so the footer rendered `codex | gpt-5.5/xhigh | runner` and suppressed the separate reasoning column.
- #395 was a resumed answer session. It found prior thread state for `issue-395-answer-default`, resumed that ACP session, and the compacted resumed log did not include a session model line. So Sepo fell back to requested `MODEL_ID=gpt-5.5`, then appended the workflow reasoning input `high`, yielding `codex | gpt-5.5 | high | runner`.

3. Root cause: mostly resumed-vs-fresh display metadata, not `followup-intent`.

The `followup-intent` gate explains why #395 had an extra portal step, but it does not control the final answer footer.

There is a related default inconsistency:

- dispatch and follow-up intent gate default to `medium`
- final answer defaults to `high`

But for these two posted comments, the final answer job used `reasoning_effort: high` in both cases. The visible mismatch came from whether the final answer run had an ACP-reported effective model (`gpt-5.5/xhigh`) or fell back to requested model plus separate reasoning (`gpt-5.5` + `high`).

One extra oddity: #396’s workflow input was still `high`, but ACP reported `gpt-5.5/xhigh`. Sepo currently trusts the ACP-reported model for display, so it surfaces that effective runtime state without reconciling it against the workflow reasoning input.

4. Recommended normalization.

Normalize before rendering the footer. For Codex GPT-5 model IDs, parse reasoning suffixes instead of suppressing the reasoning column.

Canonical footer shape should be:

```text
`codex` | `gpt-5.5` | `xhigh` | `runner`
```

not sometimes:

```text
`codex` | `gpt-5.5/xhigh` | `runner`
```

Implementation plan when approved:

1. Add a small helper near `buildModelDisplay` that decomposes Codex model IDs:
   - `gpt-5.5/xhigh` -> model `gpt-5.5`, reasoning `xhigh`
   - `gpt-5.5[high]` -> model `gpt-5.5`, reasoning `high`
   - otherwise keep existing model and reasoning fields

2. Let ACP-reported encoded reasoning override the separate env reasoning for display, because it reflects the actual effective session metadata.

3. Keep non-Codex providers unchanged.

4. Add focused tests for:
   - encoded Codex model renders as four-part footer
   - plain model plus reasoning renders as four-part footer
   - resumed/no-session-model fallback remains stable
   - non-Codex behavior is unchanged

No implementation done in this run.

---
`codex` | `gpt-5.5/xhigh` | `Macmini-runner-6`
